question: Which four metro cities are connected by India's Golden Quadrilateral highway network?
solution: The correct answer is __**Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, Kolkata**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Golden Quadrilateral (GQ)** is a highway network connecting the major metro cities of **Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata**, forming a quadrilateral shape on the map of India. • It is one of the largest highway projects undertaken in India and was initiated under the **Bharatmala Pariyojana**, which is aimed at improving connectivity and boosting economic activity. • The total length of the Golden Quadrilateral is approximately **5,846 km**, making it one of the most extensive highway networks in the world. • The project was conceptualized in **1999** and completed in phases by **2012**, with the construction and maintenance being overseen by the **National Highways Authority of India (NHAI)**. • The GQ network passes through several states and connects major industrial, agricultural, and cultural hubs, significantly enhancing trade and mobility.
